steps.intent: Introduce yourself and state the purpose of the call.
steps.action: Politely state your name and role as the claimant or their representative. Mention you are following up on an insurance claim and ask if the person can assist.

steps.intent: Confirm the other party is able to help.
steps.action: If the other party confirms, continue. If not, ask to be transferred to someone who can assist.
Restate you are calling about a specific claim. Provide claim number and other patient identifiers directly from data. Ask if they can locate the claim.

steps.intent: Gather information needed to locate the claim.
steps.action: If electronic: Request payer ID. If paper: Ask for correct mailing address. After each, confirm and proceed.

steps.intent: Identify if system issues are causing delays.
steps.action: Ask if any technical/system issues occurred that might delay claim receipt or processing.
Ask what the cutoff date is for timely claim submissions.
Ask if the patient was eligible on the date of service according to their records.

steps.intent: Determine the status of the claim.
steps.action: Ask if the claim is in process, paid, denied, or another status.

steps.intent: Collect processing details for in-process claims.
steps.action: Ask when the claim was received and the expected completion date. If delayed over 45 days, ask if it can be expedited.
Ask for dates of receipt and payment, amount paid, and claim number. Then determine if payment was via check or EFT and gather details accordingly.
Ask for check number and cashing date.
Ask for EFT number and deposit date.
Ask for denial reason/code, date, and claim number. Then ask about appeal method (mail, fax, online) and gather the relevant details.
Ask for the mailing address for appeals.
Ask for the fax number for appeals.
Ask for portal URL and instructions for submitting online appeals.

steps.intent: Wrap up the call and verify next steps.
steps.action: Thank the other party, get their name and reference number, and ask if they can help with additional claims if any.
If the conversation flow fails or information is unavailable, request escalation or ask for an alternate contact.
